title: How Living Cells Think With Electricity

teenKit.tldr: Your brain consumes half its total energy just running microscopic biological batteries that constantly pump ions across cell membranes. Without this continuous electrical hustle, consciousness and thought wouldn't even exist.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how your cells use electricity unlocks the future of treating neurological disorders, designing neuro-tech interfaces, and decoding how life actually works at the molecular level.
keyTakeaways: Your brain burns about 20 watts of power—equal to a dim refrigerator bulb—with half of that energy dedicated entirely to pumping sodium and potassium ions.
At a fundamental molecular level, the human brain is not an ethereal thought-machine, but a hard-working non-equilibrium thermodynamic engine.
Unlocking how cells use electricity required a 200-year scientific detective story featuring brutal lab rivalries, ingenious tools, and the sacrifice of thousands of shore crabs.

vocab.meaning: A heavy-duty molecular machine in cell membranes that continuously shoves sodium out and pulls potassium in using cellular energy.
An ingenious electronic lab tool used to measure and control the electrical voltage across a cell membrane to see how ions move.
An exceptionally thick nerve fiber found in squid that allowed early biophysicists to finally measure electrical signals inside a living cell.
An ultra-narrow molecular bottleneck inside an ion channel that lets specific charged atoms pass through while blocking all others.
